summary: The Awning Safety Act of 2025 requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to create a mandatory safety standard for fixed and freestanding retractable awnings within 18 months. This standard aims to protect people from death or serious injury, specifically addressing hazards such as awnings unexpectedly opening and striking someone while removing bungee tie-downs.

affected_groups.effect: Must promulgate a mandatory consumer product safety standard for retractable awnings within 18 months and determine the scope of devices covered.
Must comply with the new mandatory consumer product safety standard once it is established.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers and sellers of fixed and freestanding retractable awnings

affected_groups.effect: Receive protection from risks of death or serious injury associated with retractable awnings, such as unexpected opening while removing bungee tie-downs.

key_provisions: Requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission to issue a final consumer product safety standard for fixed and freestanding retractable awnings within 18 months of enactment.
Mandates that the standard must protect against the risk of death or serious injury related to hazards associated with retractable awnings.
Specifically targets the hazard of an awning unexpectedly opening and striking a person while they remove the bungee tie-downs for the cover.
Directs the Commission to determine which types of retractable awning devices are within the scope of the standard.
Treats the new standard as a consumer product safety rule promulgated under sections 7 and 9 of the Consumer Product Safety Act.

summary_detail.significance: The bill directs federal safety regulators to establish a mandatory rule for a specific consumer product category within a strict 18-month timeline, impacting product safety requirements for retractable awnings.
